title: Proper algebraic spaces admit proper Noetherian approximations
statement: Let $T$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to T$ be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale chart from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact, where a map is quasi-compact if its inverse image over every affine scheme test is quasi-compact. A morphism is affine if it is representable and its pullback to every affine scheme test has affine source. Here proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every base change. There is a small nonempty directed set $I$ and a compatible inverse system $f_i:X_i\to T_i$ of morphisms of algebraic spaces, with affine transition morphisms on both $X_i$ and $T_i$, such that each $T_i$ is of finite presentation over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, each $f_i$ is proper and of finite presentation, and the inverse limit of this system of arrows is $f:X\to T$. The spaces $X_i$ and $T_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Finite presentation here means quasi-compact and quasi-separated with etale chart maps locally given by finitely presented ring maps.

source.place: Tag 0A0X (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian), specialized to a scheme base; qcqs of the stages follows from finite presentation over the qcqs base Spec Z.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-space-fixed-base-fp-limit] to $f$, obtaining $X=\varprojlim_{k\in K}X_k$ over $T$ with $X_k\to T$ proper and finitely presented and transition maps $q_{lk}:X_l\to X_k$ closed immersions. Apply [prop-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system] and its definition [def-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system] to $T$. Reindex this small cofiltered system by [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] to obtain $T=\varprojlim_{j\in J}T_j$ with affine transitions and finite-type integer stages. The definition supplies that these stages are Noetherian. They are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], quasi-compact by finite type, and locally finitely presented over $\mathbf Z$ by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth]. Thus $T_j\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is finitely presented. The hypotheses of the scheme approximation hold because the given $T$ is qcqs.

source.place: Tag 0A0X (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian), proof; omitted indexing details expanded

proof.text: For each $k$, [lem-sfb-fp-space-qcqs-base-limit-descent] gives a finitely presented $Z\to T_j$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:Z\times_{T_j}T\cong X_k$. Enlarge $j$ using [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-base-eventually-proper] so that $Z\to T_j$ is proper. Further enlargement retains properness and finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. This applies over the qcqs schemes $T_j$ of step 1, not just affine bases. By [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition], $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is finitely presented. Hence $Z$ is qcqs: quasi-separatedness is exactly quasi-compactness of its absolute diagonal, and quasi-compactness follows by testing the quasi-compact structure morphism over the affine $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 0A0X (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian), proof; omitted indexing details expanded

proof.text: Form a category $\mathcal C$ with objects $(k,j,Z,\alpha)$ consisting of all the proper finitely presented models in step 2. An arrow $(l,j\prime,Z\prime,\alpha\prime)\to(k,j,Z,\alpha)$ requires $l\ge k$, $j\prime\ge j$, and a closed immersion $h:Z\prime\to Z\times_{T_j}T_{j\prime}$ whose pullback to $T$, under $\alpha\prime,\alpha$, is $q_{lk}$. Composition is composition of the closed immersions after base change. Closed immersions remain closed under base change and composition: on each scheme test this is pullback and composition of surjective ring maps on affine opens, using [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Fibre-product identifications are supplied by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Thus identities and composition satisfy the category laws and retain the required limit identifications. Take all these data in a larger universe as in [def-weil-size-convention]; they form a small category there, with no need to assume a finite or countable collection of models.

source.place: Tag 0A0X (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian), proof; omitted indexing details expanded

proof.text: The category $\mathcal C$ is nonempty by step 2. Given two objects with indices $k_1,k_2$, choose $l\ge k_1,k_2$ and a proper model of $X_l$ at a common later base stage. Apply [lem-sfb-fp-space-qcqs-base-limit-descent] to descend both maps $q_{lk_a}$ into the base changes of the two given models. Their source and target are finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Their pullbacks are closed immersions, so [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-base-descend-closed-immersion] makes both descended maps closed immersions after a common further enlargement. This gives an object mapping to both. For parallel arrows, their pullbacks agree with the same $q_{lk}$. The equality clause of the descent node makes them equal at some later base stage. Base change of their source to that stage gives an object mapping to the original source; its comparison is an isomorphism, hence a closed immersion. It equalizes the arrows. Therefore $\mathcal C$ is cofiltered. The same construction can impose any lower bound on the base index and, when both target indices are the same $k$, can keep the new $K$-index equal to $k$.

source.place: Tag 0A0X (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian), proof; omitted indexing details expanded

proof.text: Every transition $Z\prime\to Z$ in $\mathcal C$ is affine. Indeed it factors as the defining closed immersion into $Z\times_{T_j}T_{j\prime}$ followed by projection to $Z$. For an affine scheme test $W\to Z$, the latter pulls back to $W\times_{T_j}T_{j\prime}$, an affine scheme by affineness of $T_{j\prime}\to T_j$. The former then gives a closed subscheme of that affine scheme, hence an affine scheme by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This is exactly the test definition of affineness in the statement. The base transitions are affine by step 1. Thus both diagrams over $\mathcal C$ have affine transition maps.

source.place: Tag 0A0X (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian), proof; omitted indexing details expanded

proof.text: We verify the limit before reindexing. For a test space $W$, a compatible family $W\to T_j$ indexed by $\mathcal C$ determines one over $J$: every $j$ is dominated by a model from step 2, and the common refinements in step 4 make the induced map to $T_j$ independent of that model and compatible. Conversely a map $W\to T$ gives all these maps. Here the scheme limit is also the sheaf limit by [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages]. Given a compatible family $W\to Z$ indexed by $\mathcal C$, its base maps consequently give $W\to T$. Pair a component $W\to Z$ with this base map to obtain $W\to Z\times_{T_j}T\xrightarrow{\alpha}X_k$. For fixed $k$ this is independent of the model, by the common refinements with $K$-index $k$ in step 4. For $l\ge k$ the same construction of refinements with $K$-index $l$ shows that these maps commute with $q_{lk}$. Thus they give a unique $W\to X$ by the fixed-base limit of step 1. Conversely $W\to X$ gives the family by $X\to X_k\cong Z\times_{T_j}T\to Z$. The two constructions are inverse on every component and commute with maps of $W$. Hence $T$ and $X$ are the respective limits, and the compatible structure maps have limit $f$ itself.

source.place: Tag 0A0X (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian), proof; omitted indexing details expanded

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] to the diagram of arrows $Z\to T_j$ over the small cofiltered category $\mathcal C$ with the limit just verified. This produces a small nonempty directed set $I$ and the required compatible inverse system of arrows, preserving its limit. Each term is one of the models from step 2, so its base is finitely presented over $\mathbf Z$, its structural map is proper and finitely presented, and its source and target are qcqs. Each transition comes from step 5 and is affine. These are all the clauses of the item.

lean.statement: theorem exists_proper_noetherian_approximation (T : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace T] [QuasiSeparatedSpace T] (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (specULiftZIsTerminal.from T))) (hf : MapIsProper f) : ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (Xs Ts : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (fs : Xs ⟶ Ts) (πX : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ Xs) (πT : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj (schemeSpace (Over.mk (specULiftZIsTerminal.from T))) ⟶ Ts), Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk X πX)) ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk (schemeSpace (Over.mk (specULiftZIsTerminal.from T))) πT)) ∧ (∀ (i j : Iᵒᵖ) (a : i ⟶ j), MapIsAffine (Xs.map a) ∧ MapIsAffine (Ts.map a)) ∧ (∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, πX.app i ≫ fs.app i = f ≫ πT.app i) ∧ ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, MapIsProper (fs.app i) ∧ MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation (fs.app i) ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (fs.app i).hom.hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal (fs.app i).hom.hom) ∧ MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation (baseSchemeProjection (Ts.obj i)) ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (baseSchemeProjection (Ts.obj i)).hom.hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal (baseSchemeProjection (Ts.obj i)).hom.hom) ∧ (∃ (U : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ (Xs.obj i).obj.obj), CompactSpace U.left ∧ IsEtale a ∧ IsSurjective a) ∧ IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated (Xs.obj i) ∧ (∃ (V : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ (Ts.obj i).obj.obj), CompactSpace V.left ∧ IsEtale b ∧ IsSurjective b) ∧ IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated (Ts.obj i)
